# Short copies for chat

<!-- BEGIN facts -->
**Numbers you can quote** (generated by `scripts/update_readme.py` from real runs):

- Rules: 55 (26 CRITICAL/BLOCK, 21 HIGH/WARN, 8 report-only).
- 1168 tests run by default, plus 6 opt-in live-RPC tests that are skipped unless `TXWARDEN_LIVE_RPC` is set.
- Synthetic labelled evals: 2660 cases in 92 categories; accuracy 0.977 (dev 0.977, held-out 0.976); BLOCK precision 0.988, recall 0.970.
- Disagreements with the labels: 14 unsafe ALLOW and 12 over-BLOCK, of which 0 and 0 outside the deliberately ambiguous `gray_area` group. Categories with any miss: `swap_impact_band`, `swap_loose`, `swap_mid_trade_slippage_band`, `swap_slippage_band`.
- The original 122-case set still scores 0.984.
- Prompt-injection eval (a scripted model that obeys every injected instruction): 245 runs, verdict weaker than the engine's in 0, changed after `assess_risk` in 0; 50 runs ended in a fail-closed BLOCK. No real language model was run.
- Not verified: any run against a real Ethereum node, real-world detection rates.
<!-- END facts -->

## 1. Developer server, about 350 characters

TxWarden: open-source pre-signature checker for Ethereum txs. Decodes calldata, simulates on a fork,
runs deterministic rules (approvals, setApprovalForAll, hidden swap recipients, honeypots, V3
sandwich math) -> ALLOW/WARN/BLOCK. Optional LLM explains but can't change the verdict. Synthetic
evals only; live-node path not yet run against a real node. Feedback welcome: https://github.com/Intermountainh8ter/txwarden

## 2. Security channel, about 280 characters

Looking for feedback on a small OSS tx reviewer: 55 rules, fail-closed, verdict computed by code
so prompt injection can't move it (tested with a model that obeys everything it reads). Honest
caveats in the README: synthetic data, no real-node run yet, no EIP-712. https://github.com/Intermountainh8ter/txwarden

## 3. One line
